name: ShipOS – Courier NDR Resolution: WhatsApp Customer Choice, AI Reply Parsing & Shiprocket/Delhivery Actions

parameters.content:
## 🚚 ShipOS – Courier NDR Resolution on WhatsApp

For Indian D2C brands where failed deliveries quietly turn into RTOs. The courier marks "customer unavailable", nobody follows up in time, and the parcel comes back with two-way shipping charges.

### How it works
Shiprocket or Delhivery sends a tracking event when a delivery fails. The workflow works out the real reason, scores RTO risk, and messages the customer on WhatsApp with simple choices: try again tomorrow, pick a date, fix the address, give another number, or cancel. High-risk cases also alert ops in Slack.

GPT-4o-mini reads the reply in any language. Valid requests go straight to the courier's NDR API, and the customer gets a confirmation once the courier accepts. Unclear replies get a follow-up question, and tricky cases go to ops. An hourly check sends one reminder after 6 hours of silence and escalates after 20.

### Setup steps
1. Point Shiprocket and Delhivery tracking webhooks at **On Courier NDR Event**.
2. Create a Google Sheet with **Shipments** (AWB, phone, pincode, payment mode, COD amount) and **NDR Log** tabs.
3. Connect WhatsApp Business Cloud (trigger and send), Google Sheets, Slack and OpenAI.
4. Add Shiprocket as a Custom Auth credential with `{"body":{"email":"…","password":"…"}}`, and Delhivery as Header Auth (`Authorization: Token …`).
5. Replace the `REPLACE_WITH_…` IDs and send a test NDR.

## 📦 NDR Intake & Risk
Shiprocket and Delhivery tracking events land on one webhook, and only failed-delivery events go through. Each attempt is matched to its order and scored for RTO risk by reason, COD amount and attempt number. A repeat of the same attempt is ignored.

nodes.name: Sticky Note – Customer Message & Ops Alert

parameters.content:
## 💬 Customer Message & Ops Alert
The customer gets a WhatsApp explaining what went wrong, with simple reply options. The case is logged. High-risk cases, or ones with no phone number, go straight to ops on Slack.

## 🧠 Understand Reply
The reply is matched to the customer's latest open case. GPT-4o-mini works out what they want (re-attempt, new date, address fix, alternate phone or cancel) in any language. Dates outside the courier's 1–5 day window and changed pincodes are caught here.

## 🚚 Submit to Courier
Shiprocket gets a fresh auth token and then the NDR action. Delhivery gets an NDR update with its API key.

## ❓ Clarify or Escalate
Unclear replies get one follow-up question. After two tries, a new pincode or a Delhivery cancellation, ops takes over in Slack.

## ✅ Confirm Result
The courier's answer is checked and logged. If it's accepted, the customer gets a confirmation. If not, ops gets the exact error.

## ⏱️ Reply SLA Watch
Every hour, open cases are checked. Customers who haven't replied in 6 hours get one reminder. After 20 hours the case goes to ops on Slack, before the courier returns the parcel.

## 🔐 Credentials & Security
Shiprocket login and the Delhivery token live in n8n credentials, never in code. Use a dedicated Shiprocket API user. The courier webhook is open by default, so add Header Auth or a secret path. Customer addresses and phone numbers sit in your sheet, so keep it private.

nodes.name: High RTO Risk or No Phone?

values.content:
You interpret Indian e-commerce customers' WhatsApp replies about a failed delivery (NDR). Replies can be in English, Hindi, Hinglish, Telugu or Tamil, as numbers ("1") or as free text.
Options offered: 1 = re-attempt tomorrow, 2 = another date, 3 = update the address, 4 = cancel.
Resolve relative dates ("kal" = tomorrow, "parso" = day after, "Monday", "after 3 days") against TODAY in IST and return YYYY-MM-DD.
Return ONLY JSON:
{"intent": "reattempt"|"reschedule"|"update_address"|"cancel"|"alternate_phone"|"unclear",
 "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"|null, "time_window": string|null,
 "address": {"line1": string, "line2": string, "landmark": string, "city": string, "pincode": string}|null,
 "alternate_phone": string|null, "confidence": number (0-1),
 "customer_language": string, "reply_to_customer": string (max 280 chars, in the customer's language, confirming exactly what will happen; if unclear, ask ONE precise question)}
